597091.old: and a CH3 group two carbons further around the ring."

597091.note: B1. 4.2 Figure alt text, thymol: methyl "two carbons further around the ring"
597091.why: Read the usual way (OH on C1, isopropyl on C2, two carbons further = C4) this describes 2-isopropyl-4-methylphenol, not thymol. In thymol the CH3 (C5) is para to the isopropyl (C2). Screen-reader users get the wrong structure; the visible figure is correct.

597208.old: After transamination the original amino acid contains only C, H, and O.
597208.new: After transamination the original amino acid has lost its α-amino group and is now an α-keto acid.
597208.note: B6. 15.8 Lecture Connection: after transamination the amino acid "contains only C, H, and O"
597208.why: False for amino acids with N or S in the side chain (Lys, Arg, His, Trp, Asn, Gln, Cys, Met). What transamination removes is the alpha-amino group.

597217.why: The enzyme's reducing cofactor is tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4); NAD(P)H only regenerates BH4 afterward. Dropping "and NADPH" matches the section text above the table ("using O2 to add an -OH group").
